hypotheses.justification: The proof never uses `ht`. It gets `Algebra.IsAlgebraic K⟮t'⟯ M` from `AlgebraicCurve.isAlgebraic_adjoin_of_transcendental t ht'` (Theorems/Thm_AlgebraicCurve_isAlgebraic_adjoin_of_transcendental.lean). That lemma only needs `[Algebra.IsAlgebraic K⟮x⟯ F]`, which the proof derives from `[FiniteDimensional K⟮t⟯ M]` with `Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_finite`, plus transcendence of the new element (`ht'`). It needs nothing about `t`. The later steps use only algebraicity and finiteness: `t` is integral over `K⟮t'⟯`, so `K⟮t'⟯⟮t⟯` is finite over `K⟮t'⟯`; `K⟮t⟯ ≤ K⟮t'⟯⟮t⟯`; and the tower lemmas `Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite` and `Module.Finite.trans` finish. So the same proof compiles with `ht` removed. The statement also stays true without it. If `t` were algebraic over `K`, then `M` would be finite over `K`, hence algebraic over `K`, which contradicts `ht'`. That case is therefore vacuous.
